title: Stored SQLi Through the User-Agent Header
learning_objectives: Recognise that a safe, parameterised INSERT can still feed a second-order SQL injection when the stored value is later concatenated into a query
Use an HTTP request header (User-Agent) as an injection surface instead of a query-string parameter
Craft a stored UNION SELECT payload that executes on a separate read/render code path
Exfiltrate a per-container secret (settings.master_key) via the rendered analytics and exchange it for the flag
flag_hint: /solve compares ?key (or a POST key field) to settings.master_key; on match it reads the flag file at $FLAG_PATH and returns the flag, otherwise HTTP 403.
inspired_by: PortSwigger 'SQL injection in the User-Agent HTTP header' plus classic analytics-log stored/second-order SQLi patterns
